note: Short plain-English summaries of each standard, written for parents. The official wording is at the source links. 'app: false' marks standards a game cannot check on its own; 'review: true' marks standards from another grade practiced for review. Neither counts toward coverage.

sets.name: California Common Core State Standards: Mathematics

sets.name: California Common Core State Standards: English Language Arts & Literacy

sets.subject: science

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand multiplication as equal groups: 5 × 7 is 5 groups of 7.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand division as sharing equally or making equal groups: 56 ÷ 8.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Solve multiplication and division word problems within 100 (equal groups, arrays, measurements).

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Find the unknown number in a multiplication or division equation: 8 × ? = 48.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Use properties of multiplication: switch the order, regroup factors, split a factor (8 × 7 = 8 × 5 + 8 × 2).

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem: 32 ÷ 8 is the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know all products of two one-digit numbers from memory by the end of grade 3.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Solve two-step word problems with all four operations, use a letter for the unknown, and check answers with estimation.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Find patterns in numbers (odd and even, addition and multiplication tables) and explain them.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Add and subtract within 1000 fluently.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 (9 × 80, 5 × 60).

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand a fraction 1/b as one part when a whole is cut into b equal parts, and a/b as a parts of size 1/b.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Show fractions on a number line.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Explain equivalent fractions, write whole numbers as fractions, and compare fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses in grams, kilograms and liters; solve one-step word problems with them.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Draw and read scaled picture graphs and bar graphs; solve 'how many more' and 'how many less' problems.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Measure lengths to the nearest half and quarter inch and show the data on a line plot.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand area: a unit square covers 1 square unit.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Measure area by counting unit squares.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Relate area to multiplication and addition: tiling, length × width, splitting rectangles, shapes made of rectangles.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Solve perimeter problems, including finding an unknown side, and rectangles with the same area but different perimeters.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand that shapes share attributes: rhombuses, rectangles and squares are all quadrilaterals.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Split shapes into parts with equal areas and name each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Make sense of problems and keep at them.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Explain your reasoning and find mistakes in other people's reasoning.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand the digits of a three-digit number as hundreds, tens and ones.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Read and write numbers to 1000 in numerals, words and expanded form.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Compare two three-digit numbers using >, = and <.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Ask and answer questions about a story, pointing to the text for answers.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Retell stories, including fables and folktales, and find the central message or lesson.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Describe characters (traits, motivations, feelings) and how their actions move the story along.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text, literal and nonliteral.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use words like chapter, scene and stanza, and tell how each part builds on the earlier ones.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Tell your own point of view apart from the narrator's or a character's.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Explain how a story's illustrations add to what the words say.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Compare stories by the same author about the same or similar characters.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read and understand grade 2–3 literature by the end of the year (reading range over the whole year).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Ask and answer questions about an informational text, pointing to the text for answers.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Find the main idea and tell how key details support it.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Describe how events, ideas or steps connect: time, sequence, cause and effect.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Find the meaning of subject words and phrases in a grade 3 text.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use text features and search tools (headings, captions, glossary, keywords) to find information.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Tell your own point of view apart from the author's.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use pictures and maps along with the words to understand a text.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Explain how sentences and paragraphs connect: comparison, cause and effect, first/second/third.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Compare the most important points of two texts on the same topic.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read and understand grade 2–3 informational texts by the end of the year (reading range over the whole year).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read words using prefixes, suffixes and syllables, and spell common irregular words.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read aloud accurately and smoothly, with expression (checked by a grown-up: see Reading fluency in For Parents).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write opinion pieces: state an opinion, give reasons, use linking words, and end with a conclusion.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write informative texts: introduce a topic, give facts and details, use linking words, conclude.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write stories with characters, dialogue, feelings, time-order words and an ending.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Produce writing that fits the task and purpose (longer pieces, checked by a teacher).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Plan, revise and edit writing with help.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use technology to produce and publish writing.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Do short research projects.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Gather information from experience and sources, take brief notes and sort them into categories.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write routinely over short and long time frames.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Take part in group discussions, following rules and building on others' ideas.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Find the main ideas and details of a text read aloud or information presented in media.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Report on a topic or tell a story aloud with facts and details, speaking clearly.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Make audio recordings of stories or poems and add visuals.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Speak in complete sentences when the situation calls for it.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Grammar: parts of speech, plurals, abstract nouns, verb tenses, agreement, comparing, conjunctions, simple, compound and complex sentences.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Capital letters in titles, commas in addresses and dialogue, quotation marks, possessives, spelling patterns.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Choose words for effect; know the difference between spoken and written English.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Figure out unknown words from context, prefixes, suffixes, root words, dictionaries and glossaries.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Literal and nonliteral meanings, real-life word connections, shades of meaning.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Learn and use grade-level conversational, academic and subject words.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Balanced and unbalanced forces change (or do not change) how an object moves.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Observe patterns of motion to predict future motion.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Electric and magnetic forces can act between objects that do not touch.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Solve a simple design problem using magnets.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Living things have different life cycles, but all are born, grow, reproduce and die.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Being part of a group helps some animals survive.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Plants and animals inherit traits from their parents, and there is variation among them.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: The environment can influence traits.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Fossils tell us about organisms and environments of long ago.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Differences between members of the same species can help them survive, find mates and reproduce.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: In a habitat, some organisms survive well, some less well, and some not at all.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Judge solutions to problems caused when an environment changes.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Use data tables and graphs to describe typical weather in a season.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Describe climates in different regions of the world.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Judge designs that reduce the damage of weather hazards.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Define a simple design problem with criteria and limits.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Compare several possible solutions to a problem.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Plan fair tests and use the results to improve a design.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: Describe the physical and human geography of your region: maps, landforms, and how people changed the land.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: The American Indian nations of the local region, long ago and today: how they lived, used resources and passed on traditions.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: How the local community changed over time: explorers, settlers, transportation, primary sources and timelines.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: Rules and laws, the three branches of government, the Constitution, national symbols and landmarks, and American heroes.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: Goods and services, producers and consumers, choices, trade, and the skills workers need.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Capitalize holidays, products and names; use commas in letter greetings and closings.
